title: From Q&A to Getting Things Done: Doubao Launches AI Personal Assistant Xiaodou, Ending Everyday Chore Anxiety with Conversational Interaction

content_html:
Being overwhelmed every day by fragmented chores such as tracking packages, replying to messages, and keeping track of schedules is a common predicament for modern people. What we need is no longer an AI that can only "chat with us" or "retrieve information," but a digital avatar that truly understands our intent and proactively "takes action to get things done."

Recently, Doubao officially announced that its AI personal assistant, "Xiaodou," has entered invitation-only public beta. Users can try it with an invitation code and receive an exclusive free quota. This is not just the launch of a new product; it also marks the acceleration of AI applications from passive "information retrieval tools" to proactive "execution-oriented personal assistants."

Unlike traditional voice assistants, "Xiaodou" uses deep conversational interaction. Within the scope of users' explicit instructions and authorization, it precisely covers six high-frequency scenarios, aiming to bridge the "last mile" of digital life:

- Scheduling and office productivity: It supports one-click adding of to-dos and reminders by text or voice. In office scenarios, it can quickly write copy, organize thoughts, and create summaries, so workflows no longer get bogged down by trivial matters.

- Life and shopping loop: From tracking packages, finding nearby places, and searching travel guides to helping check orders, handle returns and exchanges, and answer after-sales questions, it directly steps into the service execution layer.

- Health and information protection: It provides thoughtful reminders for drinking water, taking medication, and exercise check-ins, and can respond at any time to precise queries about weather, news, and professional knowledge.

The company defines Xiaodou as "a Doubao that understands you and can proactively get things done for you." Just speak or type, and it can simplify complex processes. Its core logic is "let machines do more legwork, so people worry less."

What the industry should pay even closer attention to is the ecosystem strategy behind it. Xiaodou is currently in invitation-only public beta as a standalone product, but the capabilities and interaction experience it accumulates will gradually be fed back into and launched on the main Doubao App. This playbook of "testing a standalone assistant first + feeding core capabilities back into the main ecosystem" is steadily building ByteDance's moat in the AI personal assistant race.

The ultimate meaning of technology has never been to make humans busier, but to give time back to the people and things that truly matter. When AI learns to proactively share the burden of tedious daily tasks, we may finally be able to breathe a sigh of relief and embrace a more relaxed, freer life.
